findings.issue: The headline aggregate pools the ranks-only polynomial points (a different objective function) with the comparable ones and is dominated by them. WHAT_CHANGED §1 and cell 28 of legacy_vs_fresh.ipynb state "Across all 26 comparable points ... improves on 12, is unchanged on 8 and gets worse on 6; mean change -0.69 places", calling them comparable two lines after the same table marks the polynomial row "ranks only (additive cubic)". Recomputed from the summary rows (d_rank): the 26 points sum to -18 (mean -0.692, matches), but 11 are polynomial (headline -6; P/N -1,0,0,+2; batch -6,-5,-6,0,+3,+3) and contribute -16 of the -18. On the 15 same-target points the tally is improves 7 / unchanged 5 / worse 3, sum -2, mean -0.13 - essentially flat and 5x smaller than the quoted figure; the three largest single improvements (-6,-6,-5) are all additive-cubic-vs-degree-4 comparisons. sven_rank_summary already carries a ranks_only flag on every row; the aggregate ignores it.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the aggregate: report the tally and mean over the 15 same-target points (improves 7, unchanged 5, worse 3, mean -0.13) separately from the 11 polynomial ranks-only points, in both cell 28's print and WHAT_CHANGED §1, computing both from SUMMARY['ranks_only'] so the sentence cannot drift.

findings.issue: The "fresh rank" columns silently fall back to the TUNING-seed loss when a method's confirmation pass is not eligible, while the same row prints the confirmation loss. diff_table sets fresh_score = val_conf.where(elig_conf) then .where(notna, val_tune), and that value drives rank_fresh_common, val_fresh_rankon, the cross-scan summary's "Sven val, fresh" column and figure 2's "fresh" bars. Verified case: polynomial_scan L-BFGS - hl.confirmation_table('polynomial_scan') gives val_conf=0.485494, fin_conf=2/15, elig_conf=False, val_tune=0.239496. The exported row prints "fresh val (confirm) 0.4855 ± 0.3594" and "fresh fin/att 2/15", yet "fresh rank 11/14" and "fresh rank (all methods) 14/15", both computed from 0.2395; on the column's stated basis they would be 14/14 and 15/15. WHAT_CHANGED §4(ii) repeats it ("L-BFGS is 10th-11th on the two synthetic scans"). No marker in the table, no note in the notebook or doc, no unit test pins the fallback. Sven is eligible on all 7 scans, so no Sven rank changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the fallback (a 2-of-15 mean should not be ranked) but disclose it: mark the rank cell or add a basis column when fresh_score came from val_tune, print the substitution in cell 12, qualify the L-BFGS sentence in WHAT_CHANGED §4(ii), and add a fixture test with a mostly-diverged confirmation pass.

findings.issue: sven_only_table hardcodes grid_grew=False, so the `grid` cause can never be attributed on any of the 10 Sven-only ablations, and the rendered table shows no configuration counts at all - contradicting the module docstring's claim that causes are assigned from facts including "the per-method distinct-configuration counts". Recomputed from the records: mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression legacy = 3 configurations / 15 runs (k=64, lr=0.5, kappa 1/2/3) vs fresh = 42 configurations / 210 runs (k in {32,64} x 7 lrs x kappa 1/2/3), and the fresh winner (k=32, lr=0.75, kappa=3) does not exist in the legacy grid - yet the row reads causes `ew,droplast,split,failures` and "rel change +0.9 %" as if the level were measured on the same search. mnist_paramfrac_labelreg_scan is 19 -> 20; toy_1d_microbatch is genuinely 24 -> 24.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass grid_counts() for both sides into sven_only_table, derive grid_grew from them, and add a 'grid (leg->fresh)' column to the rendered view as the headline tables have.

findings.issue: The account never says which legacy results have no fresh counterpart. scans_in_both_roots() intersects the two roots, so everything outside the intersection disappears silently; §Scope says "27 scan directories exist in both roots: 7 headline, 4 swept, 10 Sven-only, 6 excluded" and stops. Recomputed from disk: 7 legacy scan directories have no fresh counterpart - cifar10_resnet_ce_kappaScan, cifar10_resnet_ce_paramFrac_scan, cifar10_resnet_kappaScan_labelReg, cifar10_resnet_paramFrac_scan_labelReg (the legacy Fig-5 source, now replaced by the 3-seed rebuttal_fig5_cifar_paramfrac_scan), exp_critbatch_mnist, exp_critbatch_nanogpt, exp_finetune_cifar_smallN. These back legacy paper/rebuttal figures (critical batch size, fine-tuning, CIFAR kappa and param fraction); a reader of "what the robustness fixes changed" cannot tell from this document that four of them now have no fresh data at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one cell listing legacy-only and fresh-only scan directories with a one-line disposition each (cut / replaced by <scan> / no fresh data), and a paragraph in §Scope naming the 7 and what each legacy figure now rests on.

findings.issue: The abstract is quoted with an ellipsis that removes exactly the clause in doubt, and the result is filed under "Survive". The paper (sven_submission.pdf abstract, verified verbatim) reads "On regression tasks, Sven significantly outperforms standard first-order methods including Adam, converging faster and to a lower final loss, while remaining competitive with LBFGS at a fraction of the wall-time cost." §4 quotes "converging ... to a lower final loss" and lists it as surviving, while §4(iv) of the same document retires REBUTTALS §4.6's "consistently 2nd-fastest" and §4(i) reports Sven at 63 s/epoch against 2.7-12.4 s on CIFAR. The elided word is "faster".
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the sentence whole and split the verdict: the lower-final-loss half survives on toy/polynomial/MNIST-LR, the "converging faster" half does not and must be requalified against WP2's efficiency table; likewise flag that the "fraction of the wall-time cost" half of the L-BFGS clause is not tested here.

findings.issue: The `split` cause is mis-applied to nanoGPT. Its text is "test-set-as-validation removed (MNIST 50k/10k, CIFAR 45k/5k, Shakespeare 80/10/10 by position); legacy selected and reported on the same examples", and causes_for adds it to every nanogpt row, where it is the only scan-level cause. From the records: legacy exp_nanogpt_speedrun carries n_val=871, n_train=7842 with val[0]=4.36877 at mseed5000; fresh carries n_val=871, n_train=6971, val[0]=4.36255 - the same 871 validation blocks. Legacy nanoGPT therefore did NOT select on the examples it reported; what changed is that legacy training absorbed the 871 blocks that are now the test split (and no test split existed, which is why legacy records have no `test` field). A reader of that table concludes the nanoGPT legacy numbers were test-set-selected, which is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Give nanoGPT its own code (e.g. `testsplit_carved`: a test split was carved out of legacy train, validation unchanged) or make CAUSES['split'] dataset-conditional so the nanoGPT row does not carry the 'selected and reported on the same examples' wording. Ranks are unaffected (2/5 -> 2/5).

findings.issue: Hard-coded numbers in prose that will go stale. Cell 16's closing print hard-codes "+17.8 %" and "18 -> 18 configurations" although both are computed and printed two lines above, and WHAT_CHANGED.md hard-codes the provisional CIFAR-CE cells (1.415 -> 1.424, +0.6 %, 5/6 -> 5/6, 53 %) although its opening says "Every number here is computed by analysis/legacy_vs_fresh.ipynb ... re-executing that notebook regenerates all of them" - re-executing the notebook does not update the .md. (The claims themselves check out: 0.4107 -> 0.4838 is +17.80 %, and the CIFAR-LR Sven grid is identical on both sides, k in {64,128} x lr in {0.1,0.5,1.0} x rtol in {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2}.)
findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate the computed values into cell 16's f-string, and in WHAT_CHANGED replace the CIFAR-CE numerals with a pointer to analysis/tables/legacy/legacy_diff_cifar10_resnet_ce_scan.md plus the PROVISIONAL note, or state plainly that those numerals must be re-copied after tools/select_best.py.

findings.issue: Cell 16's conclusion "it is the only method on that scan for which the BatchNorm policy changed what was being measured" contradicts the module's own CAUSES['bn'], which names "repeated forwards inside one step (Sven capture, L-BFGS closures) applied the momentum twice" - two methods, not one. Empirically the overstatement is small: at the matched legacy configuration (lr=1, max_iter=3, history_size=5) fresh CIFAR-LR L-BFGS is 0.6876 against legacy 0.6991 (-1.6 %), and the -35.6 % in the table comes from the new lr=2 point (0.4380). For Sven the matched-configuration check strengthens the claim: fresh k=64/lr=1/rtol=1e-3 is 0.7027 against legacy 0.4107 (+71 %), so the reported best-to-best +17.8 % is the conservative number.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "the only method whose validation evaluation changed" and add a matched-configuration column (legacy winner's config evaluated on both sides) for all six methods - it is the cleanest BN test and is computable from the frames already loaded.

findings.issue: Figure legibility. (a) plot_rank_slope fans equal ranks by ±0.16 against integer y-ticks, so a rank-2 point is drawn at 1.84 or 2.16 and reads off the axis as a fractional rank, with nothing on the figure saying so. (b) In the right panel the label block at ranks 1-2 overlaps itself and is crossed by connector lines ("MNIST (label reg.), P/N sweep (n_data=5000)" is struck through). (c) Neither panel marks the ranks-only points, although the largest headline move shown (polynomial 8 -> 2) and 11 of the 26 points are additive-cubic comparisons. (d) plot_method_deltas draws its "fresh (bar colour = method)" legend swatch in the first method's colour, so the legend looks like a colour key but is arbitrary; its bars sit on a log axis with a cut origin, so bar length is not proportional to value, and the panels compare legacy test-set validation against fresh held-out validation with no caveat on the figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Note the fan offset in the axis label or caption; give ranks-only points an open marker / dashed line with a legend entry; drop the meaningless legend swatch (label the grey bar only); add "legacy validated on the official test set" to figure 2's suptitle.
